item.title: Queen Elizabeth Hospital moves orthotics service to South Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Queen Elizabeth Hospital moves orthotics service to South Lynn
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has relocated its orthotics service to the health hub on Cambridge Road, off Nar Ouse Way. The team, which provides assessments and fittings for braces and splints, began operating from the new site on Monday, November 23. All adult appointments are now held at this purpose-built facility.
Hospital officials state that clinics at the North Cambridgeshire Hospital in Wisbech and the Roxburgh Unit are not affected by this change. Patients can continue to use the existing contact number, 01553 214652, for enquiries. The move follows the relocation of the hospital’s dermatology and midwifery services to the same South Lynn location.

New Lidl plans submitted for King’s Lynn site
Lidl has resubmitted plans for a new supermarket and two drive-thru units at Morston Point, near the Hardwick Retail Park in King’s Lynn. The proposal comes just weeks after West Norfolk Council rejected a previous application due to concerns regarding highway safety and access.
The updated plans include a new junction and an extension to the nearby roundabout to improve traffic flow. The supermarket would feature 117 car parking spaces and 16 bicycle bays. If approved, the store is expected to create 40 jobs, with a further 20 to 30 roles potentially added by the drive-thru units. Lidl states these changes are designed to address the specific reasons for the council's earlier refusal.

Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
Police have launched a murder investigation following the discovery of a woman’s body at a property on Alexandra Road in Wisbech. Officers were called to the scene at approximately 9:50pm on Saturday. The victim has been named as Vera. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the property on suspicion of murder and remains in custody.

Meanwhile, in West Lynn, the Reverend Andrew Davey voiced criticism over a local initiative to fund two part-time special constables. item.title: Local editors warn government over online news plans
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Local editors warn government over online news plans
Editors from across the UK, including the editor of the Fenland Citizen, have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to express concerns over proposed government plans for online news. The group argues that the suggested prominence regime is unworkable and could threaten the future of local journalism by distorting the news marketplace.
The letter highlights fears that the policy could lead to fewer local news sources for communities. Instead, the editors are calling for alternative support, such as ensuring fair payment from digital platforms and increasing government advertising spend in local titles. The signatories believe these changes are necessary to protect the sustainability of the local news ecosystem.
🔗 More details: https://www.fenlandcitizen.co.uk/news/local-editors-across-uk-warn-culture-secretary-over-unworka-9492933/

item.title: Teenager sentenced following high-speed police pursuit on A47
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Teenager sentenced following high-speed police pursuit on A47
An 18-year-old man has been handed a suspended prison sentence after a dangerous police pursuit across Norfolk. Ellis Rabey-Prosser, of Mildenhall, reached speeds of 100mph and drove the wrong way around a roundabout in Swaffham during the incident on October 6. The pursuit concluded when he crashed into a lamppost at the Hardwick roundabout in King’s Lynn.
Rabey-Prosser pleaded guilty to multiple charges, including dangerous driving and driving while disqualified. At Norwich Magistrates’ Court, he received a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for two years. He has also been disqualified from driving for a further two years and must pay £227 in costs. Police confirmed the driver had altered his vehicle's number plate before the pursuit began.

Editors from across the UK have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to express concerns over proposed government plans for online news. King’s Lynn literary lunch raises funds for local charities
A literary lunch held in King’s Lynn has raised nearly £500 for charity. Soroptimist International King’s Lynn hosted the event on Sunday, November 15, featuring guest speaker and biographer Midge Gillies. Attendees heard about the lives of pioneering female pilots, the subject of Ms Gillies' latest book, 'Atlantic Furies'.
The funds collected during the afternoon will be donated to the charities Break and GirlGuiding Lynn. Organisers hope the stories of these historic aviators will inspire young women to pursue their own ambitions.

Conservative candidate selected for Ely
The Conservative Party has announced its candidate for the upcoming election in Ely. The individual selected for the role is a councillor who previously made history by becoming the youngest person elected to the position at the age of 18. No further details regarding the candidate's identity or the specific election date have been released at this time.
